headline: Record revenue, but higher costs squeeze earnings
summary_short: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 rose 2.6% y/y to a record $651.0M, but net income fell 17.2% y/y to $102.1M and diluted EPS declined 12.5% y/y to $3.29 as higher operating costs — including unplanned downtime at Eagle Materials' Mountain Cement plant — outpaced higher sales volume.
summary_long: Revenue rose 2.6% y/y to a record $651.0M on higher volume, partly offset by lower prices. Cost of goods sold rose 9% on higher operating costs across all four segments, cutting gross margin to 25% from 29% and gross profit 13.1% y/y. Cement operating earnings fell on unplanned Mountain Cement downtime and higher maintenance costs; Gypsum Wallboard earnings fell 21% on lower prices. Net income fell 17.2% y/y to $102.1M ($3.29 diluted EPS) on lower gross profit and higher net interest expense tied to November 2025 note issuance. Eagle Materials guided fiscal 2027 capex to $490M-$525M for Mountain Cement and Duke, Oklahoma expansions. Cash fell to $233.5M after $120.8M of capex and $83.8M of buybacks; long-term debt rose to $1.74B.
